Responsibilities for treat supplies in detail
Watching the senior coordinator is the best way to learn it

This page explains why treat supplies must be handled with care at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways. When a pet traveler is anxious, a calm and appropriate treat can support comfort, cooperation, and a smoother check-in. I regret that this work is often underestimated, because small mistakes can upset both the animal and the traveler. As new staff, you should prepare supplies neatly, keep them clean, and confirm that they are suitable for the species and the journey.

Treats are never to be used as casual gifts or as a way to hurry a process. They must be offered only when the senior coordinator approves, and only after the traveler has been advised of the purpose. <<FACT F067>> A cat may refuse unfamiliar flavors, so observe closely and avoid waste or pressure. Keep supplies separated from documents, medication, and cleaning items, and report any packaging damage at once.

Bird travel requires even greater care, since health paperwork and handling notes must remain in order before any comfort item is discussed. <<FACT F083>> If a bird appears stressed, reduce noise, move slowly, and ask the senior coordinator before making any change to the plan. Do not place treats near the carrier opening unless instructed, and never allow another passenger to share food or touch the animal without permission.

When a traveler such as Isaac Tanaka or Gabriel Alvarez asks about snack use, answer calmly and direct them to the approved process. If Ollie is traveling, keep the record complete and the service respectful. Remember that careful preparation protects the pet, reassures the traveler, and supports the reputation of Aurelia Skyways.

What to remember is simple: treat supplies must be handled with patience, cleanliness, and strict attention to authorization.
